blocks.orig: 10 Days Tanzania safari, all northern parks in 1 trip!
blocks.html: Every northern park in one 10-day Tanzania safari!

blocks.orig: Explore all the glorious parks in northern Tanzania on these 10 days Tanzania Safari. From the smaller, but lovely parks Tarangire and Lake Manyara to the endless plains of the famous Serengeti and striking Ngorongoro Crater. Witness the world’s greatest wildlife spectacle, the Wildebeest Migration, in the Serengeti and enjoy the amazing views over the game-rich Ngorongoro Crater floor.
blocks.html: On this 10-day Tanzania Safari you discover all the magnificent parks of northern Tanzania. You go from Tarangire and Lake Manyara, smaller but lovely parks, to the famous Serengeti with its endless plains and the striking Ngorongoro Crater. In the Serengeti you see the Wildebeest Migration, the greatest wildlife spectacle in the world, and you take in the wonderful views over the Ngorongoro Crater floor, which is rich in game.

blocks.orig: This private safari offers you the flexibility to travel at your own pace, exactly the way you like it. You will have a private safari vehicle and guide.
blocks.html: Because this safari is private, you are free to travel at your own pace and exactly as you wish. Both the safari vehicle and the guide are yours alone.

blocks.orig: Many travelers ask us when the best time is to visit Tanzania. The answer is … there is not one right answer. It depends on what you want to see, where you want to go, your budget and interests. Please find a comprehensive guide on when is the best time to visit Tanzania here.
blocks.html: A question we hear a lot from travellers is when they should visit Tanzania. Honestly, no single answer is correct. It comes down to what you hope to see, where you would like to go, your interests and your budget. You can read our detailed guide on the best time to visit Tanzania here.

blocks.orig: Our safaris in Tanzania offer an opportunity to explore the country’s incredible wildlife and stunning landscapes. We specialize in private safaris, which means you have a 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep all to yourselves. You have the flexibility to decide when the safari starts and ends, and our experienced guides can help you make that decision on the day of your adventure. Whether you want to witness the animals at their most active during sunrise and sunset when temperatures are pleasant, or if you fancy ending the day by the pool, it’s entirely up to you. Tanzania’s diverse wildlife is active at various times of the day, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to spot the animals in action.
blocks.html: With our safaris in Tanzania you get the chance to discover the country’s remarkable wildlife and beautiful scenery. Private safaris are our speciality, so the 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep is reserved for you alone. You choose when each safari day begins and ends, and on the day itself our experienced guides are happy to help you decide. Perhaps you would like to see the animals at sunrise and sunset, when they are most active and the temperature is comfortable, or perhaps you prefer to finish the day at the pool; it’s entirely your call. Because Tanzania’s wildlife is active at different moments of the day, you’ll get many chances to watch the animals in action.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is renowned as one of the prime destinations to encounter the Big Five. These magnificent creatures—lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo—can be observed in their natural habitats, making Tanzania a preferred choice for wildlife enthusiasts.
blocks.html: Yes, definitely. Tanzania is known as one of the best places to see the Big Five. You can watch these impressive animals (lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros and buffalo) in their natural surroundings, which is why so many wildlife lovers choose Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is a safe and welcoming destination for travelers. The country offers a hospitable environment, especially in tourist areas like Arusha, and you can explore its beautiful landscapes and wildlife with confidence. Local people are friendly, and safety measures, such as keeping an eye on your belongings, are always advisable, just as you would in any other part of the world. Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people make it a fantastic place to visit.
blocks.html: Yes, definitely. Tanzania is a welcoming and safe country to travel in. Especially in tourist areas such as Arusha, the atmosphere is hospitable, and you can enjoy the beautiful scenery and wildlife with peace of mind. The local people are friendly. As anywhere else in the world, it is always sensible to take basic precautions, like keeping an eye on your belongings. Tanzania’s natural beauty and warm-hearted people make it a wonderful country to visit.

blocks.orig: As you walk out of Kilimanjaro International Airport, your personal Your Tanzania Trip guide greets you with a big smile: 'Karibu Tanzania - welcome to Tanzania!' The guide takes you straight to your hotel, where you can relax and take in the African atmosphere. The next day your guide takes you on an exclusive, private safari that allows you to travel at your own pace. Enjoy the luxury of your own safari jeep and take the liberty to stop and watch the animals as long as you like!
blocks.html: When you step out of Kilimanjaro International Airport, your personal Your Tanzania Trip guide is waiting for you with a broad smile: 'Karibu Tanzania - welcome to Tanzania!' You are driven directly to your hotel, where you can unwind and soak up the African atmosphere. On the following day your guide takes you out on an exclusive, private safari where you set the pace yourself. You have your own safari jeep, so feel free to stop and watch the animals for as long as you want!

blocks.orig: Today you will go for your first actual game drive, in Arusha National Park! This park close to Arusha is known for its abundance of tropical birds, the presence of the black and white Colobus monkey and some rare albino baboons. You will probably spot the Colobus monkey and some rare bird species such as the gorgeous Silvery Cheeked Hornbill, and, if you are very lucky, even an albino. The park also has a lake, a few craters, waterfalls, mountains, and beautiful grassy planes.
blocks.html: Today brings your first real game drive, in Arusha National Park! Located near Arusha, this park is famous for its many tropical birds, the black and white Colobus monkey and a few rare albino baboons. Chances are you will see the Colobus monkey and rare birds like the beautiful Silvery Cheeked Hornbill, and with a lot of luck even an albino. You will also find a lake, several craters, waterfalls, mountains and lovely grassy plains in the park.

blocks.orig: Tarangire National Park is well known for its big groups of elephants and the huge amount of giant baobab trees. These trees can live for hundreds of years and are actually a source of water for elephants in the dry season as they have a special technique to draw water from them. Besides, the Tarangire River is the only source of water in the dry season, which is why in this season in Tarangire you can see groups of up to 250 elephants next to many more animals!
blocks.html: Large herds of elephants and countless giant baobab trees are what Tarangire National Park is known for. A baobab can reach an age of hundreds of years, and in the dry season the elephants use these trees as a water source, thanks to a special technique for drawing water from them. In the dry season the Tarangire River is also the only water source around, so at that time of year you can see herds of up to 250 elephants in Tarangire, alongside many other animals!

blocks.orig: Lake Manyara National Park lies between Tarangire National Park and the Ngorongoro Crater, right along the 400 meters deep Great Rift Valley. The park boasts a variety of landscapes that attract many different animals. You can for example visit the lake that covers 75 percent of the park, pass through a dense rainforest with hundreds of monkeys and birds, and see elephants up close in the woodlands.
blocks.html: Situated between Tarangire National Park and the Ngorongoro Crater, Lake Manyara National Park runs right along the Great Rift Valley, which is 400 metres deep. Its varied landscapes draw a wide range of animals. You can, for instance, visit the lake, which takes up 75 percent of the park, travel through thick rainforest full of hundreds of monkeys and birds, and get close to elephants in the woodland.

blocks.orig: Serengeti National Park is widely known as the place to go on safari, mainly because of the Great Migration that passes through here. The enormous, stampeding herds are impressive, as are the vast number of predators that live here: over four thousand lions, over 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas, and hundreds of wild dogs! And of course, plenty of other beautiful animals, which your guide will be delighted to search for together with you. Are you ready for this?
blocks.html: Serengeti National Park is famous as the place for a safari, largely thanks to the Great Migration that moves through the park. The huge thundering herds are impressive, and so are the many predators living here: more than four thousand lions, more than 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas and hundreds of wild dogs! There are of course lots of other beautiful animals too, and your guide will gladly go looking for them with you. Are you ready?

blocks.orig: The famous Ngorongoro Crater is one of Africa's seven natural wonders. The crater was formed two million years ago when a vast volcano erupted. The fertile lava has created a unique ecosystem, now home to the highest concentration of animals found anywhere in Africa! Once in the crater, thousands of animals such as lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos surround you, and the views are astounding – you won’t know where to look!
blocks.html: The well-known Ngorongoro Crater counts as one of Africa's seven natural wonders. It was created two million years ago, when a huge volcano erupted. The fertile lava produced a unique ecosystem that now holds the highest density of animals anywhere in Africa! Inside the crater you are surrounded by thousands of animals, including lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos, and the scenery is stunning – you will not know where to look first!

blocks.orig: The last day! Depending on your flight time, you can relax in the lodge a bit longer before heading to Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO) for your flight home. Having second thoughts? It's also possible to add a few days to your holiday by going to one of Tanzania's paradise islands, such as Zanzibar, Pemba, or Mafia!
blocks.html: Your final day! Depending on when your flight leaves, you can relax at the lodge a little longer before driving to Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO) for your flight home. Not ready to leave yet? You can also extend your holiday by a few days on one of Tanzania's paradise islands, such as Zanzibar, Pemba or Mafia!
